title: Rate Guard and Org Key Strategy Review - HorizonLedger
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked HorizonLedger through options for organizing API keys (org-level vs project-level), configuring rate limits and quotas in the Console, and using Optimize to recommend batching/quantization. Customer cares about tiered quotas per product team, predictable cost attribution, and auditability for SOC2. Agreed next steps: run a synthetic benchmark, share security pack and pricing worksheet, and draft pilot scope.
next_steps: Samira to send pricing worksheet and security pack (by 2025-04-24)
Diego to run 1k-req/min synthetic run with HorizonLedger prompt set and share results (by 2025-04-28)
HorizonLedger to confirm pilot product teams and sample traffic (by 2025-04-25)
Schedule follow-up on pilot onboarding (tentative: week of 2025-05-05)
action_items: Diego Ramos: run synthetic benchmark (target: 1000 rps mixed chat+embed) - due 2025-04-28
Samira Patel: send pricing worksheet and SOC2 pack link - due 2025-04-24
Priya Nair: share list of product teams and expected monthly token volumes - due 2025-04-25
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-04-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Nina (Redwood Product), Priya (HorizonLedger), Tom (HorizonLedger), Elena (HorizonLedger), Marcus (HorizonLedger)
---
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Priya: Hi this is Priya, Head of Platform at HorizonLedger. We're excited — thanks for hosting.
[00:09] Tom: Tom, principal engineer.
[00:11] Elena: Elena, security.
[00:13] Marcus: Marcus, SRE.
[00:15] Samira: Great. I'll let Diego drive the demo, we'll focus today on org/project key strategy and how rate limits and quotas map to billing and multi-tenant controls. Roughly 45, 50 mins.
[00:28] Diego: Cool, pulled up the Redwood Console. First slide — we generally recommend owners choose org-level keys when you want centralized billing and coarse-grained quotas, and project-level keys when teams need isolation and per-team quotas.
[00:44] Marcus: Quick Q — can you do both? Like org-wide default and exceptions per project?
[00:49] Diego: Yeah, exactly. You can define org defaults: token quotas, rps limits, burst policies; then override at project or API key level. The routing and enforcement happen at the edge, so enforcement is consistent across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
[01:05] Tom: How do you represent burst? Sliding window? Token bucket?
[01:09] Diego: Under the hood it's token-bucket semantics — we expose window and burst params in the console: steady-state rps, burst size, and cool-down window. We ship sensible defaults, but you can tune per-project.
[01:22] Elena: For SOC2 we need audit trails when a key changes quotas or when a throttling event is hit. Is that visible?
[01:28] Diego: Yes. Audit logs capture key CRUD, quota policy changes, and rate-limit triggers. You can stream logs to your SIEM — we support GCS/S3 and direct syslog via integrations. We'll include exact retention details in the security pack.
[01:41] Samira: Also mention RBAC — you can lock quota editing to admin roles, and then team admins can only view metrics.
[01:47] Priya: Can RBAC map to our SAML groups?
[01:50] Nina: Yes, SSO through SAML/Okta maps to RBAC roles. We also support SCIM provisioning.
[01:56] Tom: Nice. From a billing standpoint, if a project exceeds its allocated quota, do we bill overage at the org level, or does Redwood refuse requests?
[02:06] Diego: There's policy options: hard enforcement will 429; soft enforcement can allow but tag tokens as billable overage. Usually customers pick hard limits for production-critical routes and soft for experimental projects. You set priority routing and fallback models too.
[02:22] Marcus: Priority routing — you mean fallback to cheaper model if primary hits quota?
[02:26] Diego: Exactly. For example you can route to an LLM-quantized variant or to a smaller model when a tier exceeds capacity; Redwood Optimize will flag likely quality regressions.
[02:37] Priya: Show us the Console flow for creating a project key with a limited quota and alerting?
[02:41] Diego: Sure. (clicks) In Projects > Keys > Create. Choose parent org, name key, attach project. Then set quota: monthly token cap, rate limit 60 rps steady with 120 burst, and alert threshold at 80% of usage.
[02:58] Diego: You can also attach tags for cost centers so billing export maps to your internal chargeback.
[03:06] Tom: Does the billing export include per-route and per-key token breakdown?
[03:10] Diego: Yes, token-level breakdowns per key and per model call. We show prompt/response tokens, and Console has CSV / BigQuery export for your finance system.
[03:20] Elena: On encryption and KMS — can keys be managed via customer-managed KMS for private?
[03:25] Diego: For Private deployments yes; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS integration for dedicated plans. We'll share the architecture diagram in the security pack.
[03:36] (short pause)
[03:40] Samira: Quick product note — Optimize can run on your historical traffic to recommend batching sizes and quantization profiles to save cost while meeting latency SLOs.
[03:49] Priya: How invasive is Optimize — does it require sending sample inputs?
[03:53] Nina: You can upload anonymized prompt sets or run in-console sampling. We never need raw PII; there are scrubbers and we can run locally in your VPC in Private mode.
[04:05] Marcus: For our multi-tenant SaaS, each customer is a project. We need to guarantee per-tenant rate limits so noisy tenants don't affect others. Is per-tenant enforcement enforced before batching?
[04:15] Diego: Yes, enforcement is at request ingress before batching. We also support prefix caching and per-tenant KV caches to partition hot contexts.
[04:23] Tom: If a tenant hits rate limit, can we auto-move them to a degraded model instead of 429?
[04:29] Diego: Yep — you can define fallback policies: degrade to smaller model, queue with retry, or 429. Policies are pluggable in the route config.
[04:36] Elena: Any way to simulate customer spike tests without affecting prod?
[04:40] Diego: We recommend a dedicated sandbox org or project. Diego: we can also run synthetic runs from our test harness; I can run a 1k rps mixed workload against your pilot config.
[04:50] Priya: That would help.
[04:52] Samira: We'll add that to action items.
[04:54] (screen share transitions to Optimize recommendations)
[05:05] Diego: Here's Optimize — it suggests batching 8 requests for typical 512 token payloads and recommends a quantized variant of the 7B model for non-critical routes. Estimated savings: 28% per-token cost for those workloads.
[05:18] Priya: Does Optimize account for tail latency impact?
[05:22] Diego: Yes, the dashboard shows latency distribution before/after simulations. It flags SLO breaches and suggests smaller batch sizes or lower quantization if latency spike risk is too high.
[05:33] Marcus: For per-project quotas, we want to ensure the meter is accurate under retries and client side backoff — are retries deduplicated?
[05:41] Diego: We support idempotency keys for dedupe at the route level; you can configure grace windows for dedupe and set how retries count against quotas.
[05:50] Tom: Let's talk numbers — our projected steady state is ~200k tokens/min across all teams, peaks up to 1.2M tokens/min during batch processing windows. How would you map that to quotas?
[06:00] Diego: You can create a high-throughput tier for product A with dedicated capacity (Dedicated pool) and soft quotas for test teams. For hosted you'll want to reserve Dedicated for the burst window or use higher-rate bursts. Also consider caching and prompt prefixing to reduce tokens for batch jobs.
[06:13] Samira: For mapping: org-level commit or reserved capacity covers baseline; projects get fractioned allocations; overflow falls back to queued/billed overage or degraded model.
[06:23] Priya: Is there a way to auto-scale quota allocations based on usage trends?
[06:27] Nina: We have autoscale policies that increase project quotas gradually based on sustained usage and guardrails to avoid cost surprises. You can trigger approvals for big jumps.
[06:35] Elena: For compliance we'll need change history and approval records.
[06:38] Diego: All of that is in audit logs and can be exported to your governance tooling.
[06:42] (brief cross talk)
[06:50] Diego: I'll open the APIs for quota config so you can script onboarding. It's REST and we also have SDK bindings.
[06:57] Tom: Any sample IaC?
[07:00] Diego: Yes, Terraform provider and examples in our docs repo. I'll drop links.
[07:05] Priya: Ok show the throttling behaviour — what does the client see on a 429 and do you include a retry-after header?
[07:12] Diego: 429 with a Retry-After in seconds, plus a structured JSON body that includes your key id and quota name that was hit. We also surface quota-remaining in response headers for better client-side handling.
[07:25] Marcus: Do you have rate-limit metrics in Console for real-time dashboards?
[07:29] Diego: Yes, per-key QPS, error rates, and top offenders. You can create alerts on any metric.
[07:35] Samira: There's a nuance — ephemeral developer keys versus long-lived production keys. We recommend ephemeral keys for dev to reduce blast radius.
[07:45] Tom: How do ephemeral keys integrate with CI/CD?
[07:48] Diego: Short-lived tokens via our token service, or you can mint session tokens with scoped quotas. Works with your CI secrets manager.
[07:55] Priya: Security question — if we want to block certain routes for a tenant entirely, can we set route-level denies?
[08:00] Diego: Route-level allow/deny rules are supported; you can attach them to keys or projects and they cascade from org down.
[08:07] (noise on line, someone mutes)
[08:15] Samira: Switching gears — demoing an edge-case: multiple projects sharing an org pool hitting concurrent bursts — show the policy resolution.
[08:24] Diego: Policy resolution order: explicit key policy > project override > org default > global default. So the most specific wins. We also have fair-share algorithms if you enable proportional rationing across projects.
[08:38] Marcus: Fair-share — is that weighted?
[08:41] Diego: Weighted. You assign weights per project and the allocator splits capacity accordingly under contention.
[08:47] Tom: Could you show the API call to set a project's quota?
[08:51] Diego: (typing) Example: POST /v1/orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/quotas with JSON body setting month_token_limit and rate_limit. I'll paste that in Slack after the call.
[09:00] Priya: On the subject of throttling spikes, do you have historical throttling analytics to retroactively find noisy tenants?
[09:07] Diego: Yes, Console has a throttling events view with snapshots of offending calls, model, and key. You can filter by tenant tag.
[09:16] Elena: We need SLA language about throttling and uptime for Dedicated pilot — is that standard?
[09:21] Samira: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency and uptime targets; we'll route you to sales ops for legal, but we can attach standard enterprise terms for pilots.
[09:31] (some side discussion about procurement)
[09:40] Tom: Hypothetical: if an internal team misconfigures and opens unlimited quota, how do we guard against cost runaway?
[09:47] Diego: We support spend caps at org and billing-account level. Also approval flows for quota increases and alerts for anomalous spend.
[09:55] Priya: Can alerts go to multiple channels? We want PagerDuty and Slack.
[09:59] Diego: Yep — Slack, PagerDuty, email, webhook.
[10:04] Samira: Alright let's walk through a quick playbook we recommend for HorizonLedger: 1) create org default with conservative quotas; 2) onboard pilot product teams using project keys and add tags; 3) run synthetic benchmark; 4) let Optimize suggest batching/quantization; 5) expand reserved capacity or Dedicated for high-throughput windows.
[10:27] Priya: That aligns. Can you include an example playbook doc?
[10:30] Samira: We'll share a playbook and onboarding checklist.
[10:33] (screen share ends)
[10:38] Diego: Quick Q from my side — what's success criteria for the pilot?
[10:42] Priya: We want to prove stable latency under 99th percentile during our mid-size peak and validate cost per 1M tokens under $X (customer redacts; internal) — also SOC2 controls in place.
[10:55] Samira: Good. We'll map those to the pilot acceptance tests.
[11:00] Tom: Anything else on routing policies? One more question — can tenant-level quotas interact with model version pins? If a pinned model is expensive and hits org limit, will the pin block fallback?
[11:10] Diego: You can set pin as mandatory or soft-pin. Soft-pins allow fallback under capacity pressure; mandatory pins will surface 429s or queue. You choose per-route.
[11:20] Elena: For security review we'll want the network architecture diagram and KMS flow.
[11:23] Samira: We'll include that in the security pack.
[11:26] (short pause)
[11:30] Samira: Ok recap — action items and next steps, Diego will run synthetic run, I'll send pricing and security docs, Priya will share teams and volumes. We'll aim to meet again after Diego's run.
[11:42] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[11:44] Samira: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[11:48] (call ends)
